title: Running the waste route in a fixed order
audience: Cleaners carrying out a waste route through an office, shared building or turnover site.
learningOutcomes: Describe the order of a waste route from the storage room to the drop point.
Empty, reline and check each desk bin and sanitise each touch point in turn.
Identify when a bin, area or item has been missed and correct it before leaving the floor.

instruction.heading: Starting and moving through the space
instruction.body: Begin with a check of your protective equipment and the kit, then move through the area in a steady loop. Keep to one direction on every pass so that no desk is skipped. Hold the bin close to your body and do not let it drift out to the side. Where corridors and cubicles branch off, work in short zig-zags, finishing each row before you move on, so you do not double back.

instruction.heading: At each desk
instruction.body: Empty the desk bin into the collection bin, check that spare liners are in its base, and fit a fresh liner if one is needed. Replace a liner that is torn, wet or holding food. Wipe the desk top with a sanitised cloth, lifting only what you need to lift. Pick up loose rubbish around the bin and beneath the desk. If a chair or the bin itself has to move to reach under the desk, put it back before you leave.

instruction.heading: Touch points and small items
instruction.body: Items people touch often, like switches, handles and push plates, are sanitised with a cloth kept only for that job. Empty pencil sharpeners and punches as you pass them. Leave boxes and stacked items where they are, unless they are clearly marked for disposal. Ask the site contact before you move anything of value.

instruction.heading: Finishing the route
instruction.body: Once the collection bin reaches capacity, knot the bag shut and set it on the drop sheet at the designated point. Return the kit to the storage room, place used cloths in the laundry basket, and set the kit up for the next visit.

procedure: Check your protective equipment and the kit.
Move in one consistent direction, working row by row.
At each desk, empty the bin, check and replace the liner, then wipe the desk top.
Clear loose waste from around the bin and beneath the desk.
Sanitise each touch point with its own cloth.
Empty sharpeners and punches as you pass them.
Set full bags on the drop sheet at the designated point.
Return the kit and place used cloths for laundering.

workedExamples.situation: On a floor of sixty desks, a cleaner finds a bin holding food at desk 34 and an empty bin at desk 35.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What should be done with each bin?
workedExamples.reasoning: The food bin is emptied and its liner is replaced, because food in a bin means the liner must go. The soiled base is wiped if needed. The empty bin still gets a liner check, and its spare liners are confirmed. If the site card says the food bin fills quickly, use an extra liner layer there, as the site allows.

equipmentAndPpe: Desk cloths and a separate touch-point cloth

commonErrors.error: Missing bins under desks or in side areas.
commonErrors.prevention: Work row by row and check the bin list on the site card.

commonErrors.error: Moving personal items to reach a bin.
commonErrors.prevention: Work around personal items. If a bin is blocked, ask the owner before moving anything.

commonErrors.error: Leaving a liner loose in the bin.
commonErrors.prevention: Seat and tie the liner before moving to the next desk.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Keep a full bin close and under control. Do not carry it against the body with the arms stretched out.
Sharp items can be hidden in waste. Wear gloves and do not reach into a bin without looking.

qualityStandard: Every bin on the route is emptied, relined and seated.
No loose waste is left around or under desks.
Touch points are sanitised and dry.
documentationEvidence: Route completion recorded on the site record.
Any missed area or issue noted with its location.
summary: Work in one direction so no area is skipped or visited twice.
At each desk: empty, check and replace the liner, wipe the top, pick up loose waste.
Use a dedicated cloth for touch points, and never reach into a bin blind.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should the route move in one consistent direction?
options: So no area is skipped or visited twice
Because the client asked for it
To make the collection bin heavier

knowledgeChecks.question: A desk bin holds food. What should happen to its liner?
options: Shake the food down and leave the liner in for the next visit
Replace it, because food in the bin means the liner must go
Leave it until the next scheduled visit to be cleared

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you use to sanitise a touch point such as a light switch?
options: The cloth used for the desk top
A cloth kept only for touch points
Nothing, since switches are not surfaces
